# Temple Scroll Column 13 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 13 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 13:2 — "gather in the produce" vs. "harvested the crops"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "when you gather in the produce of the land" | Literal be-ospekhem et tevuat ha-aretz |
| LOGOS | "when you have gathered the produce of the land" | Standard formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "after you have harvested the crops of the land" | "Harvested" and "crops" more natural in modern English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Gathered the produce" is accurate and clear. PNEUMA's "harvested the crops" narrows the meaning — tevuah includes all produce, not only harvested crops. EMET's "gather in" is slightly archaic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 13:5 — "Festival of Booths" vs. "Festival of Shelters" — chag ha-sukkot

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a festival of booths" | Literal; lowercase as common noun |
| LOGOS | "the Festival of Booths" | Standard scholarly name; capitalized as proper festival name |
| PNEUMA | "the Festival of Shelters" | "Shelters" conveys the actual living arrangement more clearly |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Festival of Booths" (LOGOS). This is the universally recognized English name for Sukkot in biblical scholarship and Jewish tradition. "Shelters" (PNEUMA), while descriptively accurate, would confuse readers familiar with the standard terminology. Capitalized as a proper festival name.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 13:7 — "sons of a year" vs. "yearling" vs. "one-year-old" (recurring)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "lambs, sons of a year" | Literal bene shanah |
| LOGOS | "yearling lambs" | Standard convention |
| PNEUMA | "one-year-old lambs" | Most transparent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "yearling" (LOGOS), consistent with Column 11 ruling.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Consistent with established precedent.

---

## 13:12 — "dwell in booths" vs. "live in shelters"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you shall dwell in booths" | Literal teshvu ba-sukkot |
| LOGOS | "you shall dwell in booths" | Same as EMET; "dwell" appropriate for ritual dwelling |
| PNEUMA | "You are to live in shelters" | "Live" and "shelters" more natural |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "dwell in booths" (EMET/LOGOS). "Dwell" captures the ritual, temporary nature of sukkah-dwelling better than "live," which implies permanent residence. "Booths" consistent with the festival name.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 13:14 — "caused to dwell" vs. "made dwell" vs. "had live"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "in booths I caused the sons of Israel to dwell" | Literal Hif'il of yashav; preserves word order |
| LOGOS | "I made the children of Israel dwell in booths" | Standard English word order; "made dwell" for Hif'il |
| PNEUMA | "I had the Israelites live in shelters" | Most natural modern phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Made... dwell" is an acceptable English rendering of the Hif'il causative. "Children of Israel" preferred over PNEUMA's "Israelites" for the formal register of divine speech.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 13:16 — "perpetual statute" vs. "lasting requirement" (recurring)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a statute forever throughout your generations" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "a perpetual statute throughout your generations" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "a lasting requirement for all your generations" | Accessible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS, consistent with Columns 11 and 12 rulings.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Consistent with established precedent.

---
